summary: pi is a well-modularized monorepo whose coding-agent CLI (~59k LOC across 199 files) already ships a first-class rebrand mechanism: a single `piConfig` block in packages/coding-agent/package.json drives APP_NAME/APP_TITLE/CONFIG_DIR_NAME/bin, which then propagate through ~13 call sites (env var names, TUI title, help text, update messages) — so renaming pi->strape is a ~1-file, few-line fork, not a repo-wide edit. Separately, the two 'reuse Claude Code files' asks are already solved with zero code changes: CLAUDE.md is a built-in AGENTS.md fallback (resource-loader.ts:71) checked while walking cwd ancestors, and docs/skills.md explicitly documents pointing settings.json's `skills` array at `~/.claude/skills` and `.claude/skills`. For a Grok+OpenAI-only harness, xAI and OpenAI are both built-in, OAuth-capable providers in pi-ai reusing one shared OpenAI-compatible client, so no custom-provider extension is required; the real supply-chain cost is that pi-ai statically imports @anthropic-ai/sdk, @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime, @google/genai and @mistralai/mistralai for the ~40 providers strape won't use, and pi-client/pi-protocol/pi-server/session-backends/evals are dead weight for a local terminal CLI (unused by the CLI runtime, only wired to an unfinished 'server' subcommand and to a library-only RemoteSession export). The repo already has offline-conscious tooling (build:offline, npm-shrinkwrap generation, pinned-deps check, committed root package-lock.json, local-release.mjs for tarball-based non-npm-registry installs) that strape can adopt as-is; the one real gap is that packages/ai/src/providers/data/ (model pricing/catalog JSON) is gitignored and must be network-hydrated at least once before a from-source build succeeds.
key_facts: Bin/package names: coding-agent package.json:9-11 `"bin": {"pi": "dist/cli.js"}`, name `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`; pi-ai package.json also exposes a `pi-ai` bin (packages/ai/package.json).

Branding is centralized via a package.json field: packages/coding-agent/src/config.ts:487-496 reads `pkg.piConfig?.name` and `pkg.piConfig?.configDir` from the package's own package.json (packages/coding-agent/package.json:6-8 `"piConfig": {"configDir": ".pi"}`) to derive APP_NAME (default 'pi'), APP_TITLE, CONFIG_DIR_NAME (default '.pi'), and even the env var names ENV_AGENT_DIR/ENV_SESSION_DIR = `${APP_NAME.toUpperCase()}_CODING_AGENT_DIR` — config.ts:494 literally comments 'e.g., PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR or TAU_CODING_AGENT_DIR', evidence upstream already designed this for downstream forks/rebrands.

APP_NAME/APP_TITLE are consumed (not re-hardcoded) in ~13 files: cli.ts:8-12 (process.title), main.ts, slash-commands.ts:41, export-html/index.ts:277/311, cli/args.ts (help/usage text, ~25 lines), package-manager-cli.ts (install/update UX), interactive-mode.ts (logo, terminal title, update prompts), rpc-entry.ts, bun/cli.ts, first-time-setup.ts:56, tools-manager.ts:112 (User-Agent header) — i.e., the CLI's user-facing text is already parameterized, not scattered literals.

Explicit fork/rebrand awareness in code: packages/coding-agent/src/cli/startup-ui.ts:26-42 defines OFFICIAL_PACKAGE_NAME/OFFICIAL_APP_NAME/OFFICIAL_CONFIG_DIR_NAME and `isOfficialDistribution()`; `shouldRunFirstTimeSetup()` (startup-ui.ts:115-131) explicitly disables the first-run wizard '(not a fork/rebrand)' when the check fails — this is the only functional gate on rebranding found; no other feature checks it.

One un-parameterized literal string survives: system-prompt.ts:121 hardcodes 'You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness' and system-prompt.ts:131-138 say 'Pi documentation' — these do NOT use APP_NAME, so a stock rename via piConfig alone still self-identifies as 'pi' to the model; a real rename needs this one string patched too.

CLAUDE.md is already a supported context file: resource-loader.ts:71 `const candidates = ["AGENTS.override.md", "AGENTS.md", "AGENTS.MD", "CLAUDE.md", "CLAUDE.MD"]`, consumed by loadProjectContextFiles() (resource-loader.ts:118-156) which walks from cwd up to filesystem root (one file per directory) plus a global one at agentDir — this already works today, no config or fork needed for project-level CLAUDE.md reuse. Global CLAUDE.md reuse would need agentDir (~/.pi/agent by default) to contain a CLAUDE.md, e.g. via a manual symlink, since agentDir != ~/.claude.

Skills reuse from Claude Code is an officially documented feature, not a hack: docs/skills.md lines ~40-62 'Using Skills from Other Harnesses' shows adding `{"skills": ["~/.claude/skills", "~/.codex/skills"]}` to global settings.json and `{"skills": ["../.claude/skills"]}` to `.pi/settings.json` for project-level Claude Code skills — settings.md:233-248 documents the same `skills`/`extensions`/`prompts`/`themes` string[] resource-override settings.

Native pi skill dirs are gated by CONFIG_DIR_NAME: resource-loader.ts:812-821 `join(this.cwd, CONFIG_DIR_NAME, "skills"|"prompts"|"themes"|"extensions")`; there is also a second, independent, non-renameable convention hardcoded as literal `.agents` (not tied to CONFIG_DIR_NAME): trust-manager.ts:186/195 and package-manager.ts:442/2375/2415/2466 read `.agents/skills` (project, walking to git root) and `~/.agents/skills` (global) — this is the emerging agentskills.io cross-tool standard, distinct from Claude Code's actual `.claude/skills` location.

Risk if CONFIG_DIR_NAME is set to '.claude' via piConfig instead of using the documented settings.json approach: settings-manager.ts:201 would then read/write project settings at `cwd/.claude/settings.json` — the exact path Claude Code itself uses for project settings, with an incompatible schema — a real collision risk. Safer path per skills.md is to leave CONFIG_DIR_NAME as '.pi' (or a fresh '.strape') and use the settings.json `skills` array to point at `.claude/skills`/`~/.claude/skills` explicitly.

PI_* env vars found in coding-agent/src (verbatim, not all APP_NAME-derived): PI_CLEAR_ON_SHRINK, PI_CODING_AGENT, PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR, PI_EXPERIMENTAL, PI_HARDWARE_CURSOR, PI_HOST, PI_KEY, PI_MODEL, PI_OFFLINE, PI_PACKAGE_DIR, PI_PROVIDER, PI_REASONING_LEVEL, PI_SESSION_FILE, PI_SESSION_ID, PI_SHARE_VIEWER_URL, PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK, PI_STARTUP_BENCHMARK, PI_TELEMETRY, PI_TIMING, PI_VERSION — config.ts:369 `PI_PACKAGE_DIR` is a literal string (not APP_NAME-derived), intended for Nix/Guix store paths, not a rebrand hook.

Package purposes (from each package.json 'description' + dependency graph, all v0.84.0): pi-tui = TUI rendering (0 internal deps, deps: get-east-asian-width, marked); pi-telemetry = telemetry contracts/schema only, ships a no-op implementation (packages/telemetry/src/noop.ts), no network code itself; pi-ai = 'Unified LLM API' (deps: @anthropic-ai/sdk, @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime, @google/genai, @mistralai/mistralai, openai, plus pi-telemetry); pi-agent-core = 'General-purpose agent with transport abstraction, state management, attachment support' (deps: pi-ai, pi-telemetry, diff, ignore, yaml); pi-protocol = 'Transport-neutral CBOR protocol for remote pi sessions' (dep: typebox only); pi-client = 'Transport-neutral client for remote pi sessions over framed CBOR bytes' (dep: pi-protocol only); pi-server = 'experimental server package for pi' (deps: pi-ai, pi-protocol); pi-session-backend-sqlite-node = 'Node sqlite session backend for pi-agent-core sessions'; pi-evals = private, vitest-evals based agent-quality eval harness (devDependency-only, no runtime deps).

coding-agent's actual runtime dependency closure (packages/coding-agent/package.json 'dependencies') = pi-agent-core, pi-ai, pi-client, pi-protocol, pi-tui, plus non-workspace libs (chalk, cross-spawn, diff, glob, grok-mermaid, highlight.js, hosted-git-info, ignore, jiti, minimatch, proper-lockfile, semver, typebox, undici, yaml, @silvia-odwyer/photon-node). pi-server and the sqlite session backend are NOT dependencies of coding-agent at all and are not imported by anything outside their own package (grep for '@earendil-works/pi-server' across the repo only matches its own package.json; sqlite-node only referenced in its own test-utils.ts).

pi-client/pi-protocol usage inside coding-agent is confined to packages/coding-agent/src/client/remote-session.ts and transcript.ts, re-exported via the package's `./client` export subpath (package.json:19-25) as an SDK-only surface — grep shows `RemoteSession(` is never instantiated by the CLI's own cli.ts/main.ts/interactive-mode.ts; it exists for embedding into a would-be remote/companion client and is otherwise dead weight for a plain local terminal CLI.

The CLI's own 'server' subcommand (packages/coding-agent/src/cli/experimental/commands/server.ts) is scaffolding: it defines a `runServer()` context interface but `runServer` has zero implementations in the tree (grep for `runServer` matches only the interface declaration and its one caller site in cli/experimental/cli.ts) — the remote-server feature is unfinished/unwired, reinforcing that pi-server + pi-client + pi-protocol + sqlite backend are safely droppable for a minimal local CLI.

xAI/Grok and OpenAI are both built-in first-class providers, not extensions: packages/ai/src/providers/xai.ts and openai.ts registered in packages/ai/src/providers/all.ts:91-124; xAI reuses the shared OpenAI-compatible client (packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts:1465/1487 `provider === "xai"` / `isGrok = provider === "xai" || baseUrl.includes("api.x.ai")`), which itself imports the `openai` npm SDK (openai-completions.ts:1 `import OpenAI from "openai"`) — xAI needs no dedicated SDK dependency. Both support OAuth subscription login (docs/providers.md lines 42-45, 22) in addition to API keys (XAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY).

Supply-chain surface from unused providers: packages/ai/src/providers/all.ts:5-42 statically imports (top-level `import`, not dynamic `await import()`) every provider module including anthropic-messages.ts (`@anthropic-ai/sdk`), bedrock-converse-stream.ts (`@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime`, `@smithy/node-http-handler`), google-*.ts (`@google/genai`), mistral-conversations.ts (`@mistralai/mistralai`) and calls every provider factory unconditionally in one array (all.ts:91-124) — these SDKs load into memory and ship as hard npm dependencies of pi-ai (packages/ai/package.json dependencies) even for a Grok/OpenAI-only deployment; restricting via settings.json `enabledModels` (e.g. `["gpt-*","grok-*"]`, documented settings.md:293) hides them from the UI/model catalog but does not remove them from the dependency tree or from what gets loaded at process start.

Extension API confirms provider/branding boundaries: docs/extensions.md:1705-1835 documents `pi.registerProvider(name, config)` / `pi.unregisterProvider(name)` as a runtime extension hook (used by examples/extensions/custom-provider-anthropic and custom-provider-gitlab-duo) — but there is no equivalent extension hook to change APP_NAME/CONFIG_DIR_NAME at runtime; those are read once from the shipped package.json before extensions load (config.ts:479-491), so true branding requires editing that one file, not an extension.

getPackageDir() (config.ts:367-388) — which supplies the package.json read for piConfig, plus themes/docs/examples/README/CHANGELOG/assets paths — walks up from the coding-agent module's own __dirname (or `dirname(process.execPath)` for the Bun binary), not from the invoking script or a wrapper's directory; the only override is `PI_PACKAGE_DIR` (config.ts:369, intended for Nix/Guix store-path issues) which would have to point at a directory mirroring the entire dist/ asset layout. Conclusion: a thin wrapper npm package that merely `require()`s/execs pi-coding-agent's dist/cli.js CANNOT change APP_NAME/CONFIG_DIR_NAME/bin without either forking that one package.json or reproducing its whole asset tree — a light fork of packages/coding-agent/package.json (~5-10 line diff to name/bin/piConfig, low upstream-merge-conflict risk since upstream rarely touches those lines) is the realistic path to a real rename, not a pure-wrapper/no-fork approach.

Dogfooding evidence: repo root has its own `.pi/` (extensions/, skills/, git/, npm/, prompts/) used to develop pi with pi itself, and a tracked dev-run script `pi-test.sh` (repo root, `git ls-files pi-test.sh` confirms tracked) that runs `tsx ... packages/coding-agent/src/cli.ts` directly from source with no build step — directly reusable pattern for a strape dev loop (e.g. copy to `strape-test.sh`).

Build pipeline: root package.json scripts `build` (full, includes packages/ai's `generate-models` which hits the network to refresh model metadata) vs `build:offline` (skips generation, chains `tui->telemetry->ai:build:offline->agent->session-backends/sqlite-node->protocol->client->server->coding-agent`); packages/ai/package.json scripts show `build:offline` = `check:model-data && tsgo -p tsconfig.build.json && ... cp -r src/providers/data dist/providers/data`.

Offline-build caveat: `packages/ai/src/providers/data/` (per-provider model/pricing JSON, e.g. xai.json/openai.json consumed by packages/ai/src/providers/xai.models.ts:4) is gitignored (root .gitignore:11 `packages/ai/src/providers/data/`) and does NOT exist in a fresh clone of this repo (verified: directory absent, node_modules present but no dist/ built yet) — `check:model-data` (packages/ai/scripts/check-model-data.ts) fails with 'Model data is missing or stale. Run `npm run hydrate:model-data`' until that data is hydrated once via network (root script `hydrate:model-data`) or copied from a previously-published npm tarball (pi-ai's package.json `files: ["dist", "README.md"]` ships `dist/providers/data` in every published release). So 'build fully offline from the git tree' is true only after one prior network-dependent hydration (or by seeding the data directory from an npm-installed copy); it is not offline on a bare clone with zero prior state.

Supply-chain tooling already present and reusable as-is: root package.json `check:pinned-deps` (scripts/check-pinned-deps.mjs enforces exact-version pins for all non-workspace deps across every package.json), `check:shrinkwrap`/`shrinkwrap:coding-agent` (scripts/generate-coding-agent-shrinkwrap.mjs, derives packages/coding-agent/npm-shrinkwrap.json from the committed root package-lock.json, with an explicit `allowedInstallScriptPackages` allowlist e.g. `@google/genai@1.52.0`, `protobufjs@7.6.5`), `check:install-lock:coding-agent` (scripts/generate-coding-agent-install-lock.mjs, produces a minimal install-time lockfile under packages/coding-agent/install-lock/), committed `package-lock.json` at repo root plus 6 more lockfiles (`git ls-files` shows 7 total *package-lock.json/npm-shrinkwrap.json files), and a `.github/workflows/npm-audit.yml` CI job.

scripts/local-release.mjs already implements exactly the 'build+pack+install locally without publishing to the public npm registry' workflow strape needs: it lists the 9 publishable packages (telemetry, ai, tui, agent, protocol, client, sqlite-node backend, server, coding-agent), builds/packs tarballs, and creates isolated local installs outside the repo (`--skip-install`, `--skip-bun-install`, `--force` flags) for release testing — directly reusable for a private strape build with zero registry publication.

Phone-home/network surface for security review: docs/settings.md:81/83 — `enableInstallTelemetry` gates an anonymous ping to `https://pi.dev/api/report-install`; independent of that, pi always attempts to fetch `https://pi.dev/api/latest-version` for update checks unless `PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK=1`; `--offline` / `PI_OFFLINE=1` disables all such startup network calls at once. `getShareViewerUrl()` (config.ts:502-508) also defaults to `https://pi.dev/session/` for the session-share feature, overridable via `PI_SHARE_VIEWER_URL`.

Branding string-surface size estimate: 469 files repo-wide reference the `@earendil-works/pi-` npm scope (import specifiers across the whole monorepo — this is what a full npm-scope rename would touch, i.e. scattered/high-effort and low-value unless strape actually publishes packages), vs only ~13 files in coding-agent/src consume the centralized APP_NAME/APP_TITLE constants (low-effort, high-value for user-facing rebrand), vs 1 file (system-prompt.ts:121) with an un-parameterized literal 'pi' string meaningfully affecting the model's self-identification.

Repo size for security review scoping: packages/coding-agent/src = 199 files / ~58.7k LOC; packages/ai/src = 174 files / ~22.4k LOC; packages/agent/src = 48 files / ~12.2k LOC; packages/tui/src = 38 files (not counted for LOC). SECURITY.md at repo root explicitly states Pi has no sandbox by design, treats the local user's own filesystem/env as inside the trust boundary, and calls out AGENTS.md/skill/extension content as an inherent, unmitigated prompt-injection vector — relevant baseline for strape's own security review scope.
risks: Setting CONFIG_DIR_NAME to '.claude' (instead of using the documented settings.json `skills` array) would make pi's own project settings.json live at `cwd/.claude/settings.json` — the same path and filename Claude Code uses for its own project settings, but with an incompatible schema; this could silently corrupt or be corrupted by Claude Code project configuration in any repo used with both tools.

Global CLAUDE.md reuse is not automatic: pi's global context-file lookup uses `agentDir` (default `~/.pi/agent`), not `~/.claude`, so a user's existing Claude Code global CLAUDE.md at `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` will not be picked up without a manual step (e.g., symlink) even though project-level CLAUDE.md reuse works with zero configuration.

A pure 'thin wrapper package, no fork' strategy cannot achieve a real pi->strape rename: APP_NAME/CONFIG_DIR_NAME/bin are all sourced from packages/coding-agent's own shipped package.json, resolved via getPackageDir() walking up from that package's own __dirname/execPath — not overridable by a wrapper's package.json or by any documented env var. Any real rename requires forking (even minimally) packages/coding-agent/package.json.

Restricting providers via `enabledModels` in settings.json only hides unused providers from the UI; it does not shrink the actual dependency tree — @anthropic-ai/sdk, @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime, @google/genai, and @mistralai/mistralai remain installed and are statically loaded into the process at startup via pi-ai/src/providers/all.ts's unconditional imports, so they remain part of the supply-chain attack surface for a nominally 'OpenAI/xAI-only' deployment unless pi-ai itself is forked to remove the unused provider modules from all.ts.

A from-source 'offline' build is not truly zero-network on a fresh clone: packages/ai/src/providers/data/ (model catalog/pricing JSON) is gitignored and must be hydrated via a network call (`npm run hydrate:model-data`) or sourced from a previously published npm tarball before `build:offline` will pass its `check:model-data` gate — a genuinely air-gapped first build needs this data pre-seeded.

pi silently makes outbound calls to pi.dev (update-version check, install telemetry, session share viewer URL) unless explicitly disabled via `--offline`/`PI_OFFLINE=1`/`PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK=1`/settings — a security-conscious fork should decide and hardcode strape's own default posture here rather than inherit pi.dev's defaults silently.

The unfinished `server` subcommand (cli/experimental/commands/server.ts) and pi-client/pi-protocol's RemoteSession SDK surface are unused-but-shipped attack surface in a plain local-CLI deployment; leaving them in place is low-risk (small, no-SDK dependencies, not wired to any listener by default) but is dead code that a from-scratch security review would need to explicitly rule in/out of scope.

SECURITY.md explicitly disclaims sandboxing and treats AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/skills/extensions content as an unmitigated prompt-injection vector and treats local filesystem write access as already inside the trust boundary — reusing arbitrary pre-existing Claude Code skills/extensions from other projects inherits this same trust model; skills.md itself warns 'Skills can instruct the model to perform any action... Review skill content before use.'
recommendations: Do not rename the internal npm workspace package names/scope (@earendil-works/pi-*, touches ~469 files) — there is no value for a private, unpublished fork and it would create a permanent, ever-growing upstream-merge-conflict surface. Reserve renaming for the single user-facing surface: packages/coding-agent/package.json's `bin` key (`pi`->`strape`) and `piConfig` block (`name: "strape"`, keep or repick `configDir`), plus optionally patch the one literal string in system-prompt.ts:121/131-138 so the model self-identifies as strape. This is a ~1-2 file, low-conflict-risk diff to maintain against every upstream pull.

For CLAUDE.md/.claude/skills reuse, do NOT change CONFIG_DIR_NAME at all initially — ship it as pure configuration per docs/skills.md: add `"skills": ["~/.claude/skills"]` to global settings.json and `"skills": ["../.claude/skills"]` to the project-local settings.json. Project CLAUDE.md already works with zero configuration (resource-loader.ts:71). For global CLAUDE.md reuse, symlink `~/.pi/agent/CLAUDE.md` (or `~/<configDir>/agent/CLAUDE.md` if configDir is renamed) to the existing `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. This achieves the entire goal-4 ask with zero source changes, which should be validated first before any forking work begins.

If CONFIG_DIR_NAME is renamed at all, rename it to something strape-specific and non-colliding (e.g. `.strape`) rather than `.claude`, specifically to avoid the settings.json/commands schema collision documented above; keep `.claude/skills` and `.claude/CLAUDE.md` reuse purely additive via the settings.json `skills` array and the built-in CLAUDE.md fallback, never by aliasing pi's own config root onto `.claude`.

For the minimal Grok+OpenAI CLI, keep the monorepo structure and internal dependency graph as-is (pi-tui, pi-telemetry, pi-ai, pi-agent-core, pi-coding-agent) but explicitly exclude/never build pi-client, pi-protocol, pi-server, session-backends/sqlite-node, and pi-evals from strape's build/workspace list — none are needed by the CLI runtime (evidence: server unwired, client/protocol only used by an unreferenced RemoteSession SDK export, sqlite backend referenced nowhere outside its own tests). This shrinks the build graph and the security-review surface without touching any shared logic, so it stays trivially re-appliable on every upstream pull (it's a workspace/script-list change, not a code change).

Treat the pi-ai provider bloat (Anthropic/AWS Bedrock/Google GenAI/Mistral SDKs) as the primary, and only meaningfully forkable, security-surface reduction: either (a) accept it as-is for maintainability (lowest effort, matches goal 5) and rely on `enabledModels` glob restriction plus normal `npm audit`/lockfile pinning for risk management, or (b) fork only packages/ai/src/providers/all.ts to remove unused provider imports/registrations (moderate, ongoing merge-conflict risk on a file that does change somewhat often upstream as new providers are added) — recommend (a) unless a specific audit finding on one of those SDKs forces (b).

Adopt the existing offline/reproducibility tooling wholesale rather than reinventing it: use `npm install --ignore-scripts`, `npm run check:pinned-deps`/`check:shrinkwrap`/`check:install-lock:coding-agent`, the committed root `package-lock.json`, and `scripts/local-release.mjs` to produce a private, non-npm-registry-published strape build/tarball. Before relying on a from-scratch offline build, run `npm run hydrate:model-data` once (or seed `packages/ai/src/providers/data/` from a published `@earendil-works/pi-ai` tarball) since that directory is gitignored and required by `build:offline`'s `check:model-data` gate.

Set strape's default network posture explicitly and document it (equivalent of `PI_OFFLINE=1`/`PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK=1`/`enableInstallTelemetry: false` baked into strape's default settings.json) rather than inheriting pi.dev's default phone-home behavior (update-version check, install telemetry, session-share URL all point at pi.dev by default per settings.md:81-83 and config.ts:502-508).

Reuse `pi-test.sh` verbatim (copy/rename) as strape's dev-loop entry point (`tsx` running `packages/coding-agent/src/cli.ts` directly) — it already supports an `--no-env` mode that strips all provider API keys/OAuth env vars, useful for strape's own auth testing across OpenAI/xAI.

Scope the security review to: (1) packages/coding-agent/src (~58.7k LOC, the actual command surface: bash/edit/write tools, extension loader, package manager/installer, session persistence), (2) packages/ai/src (~22.4k LOC, but focus specifically on openai.ts/openai-completions.ts/openai-responses.ts/xai.ts and the shared HTTP/streaming plumbing since those are the only providers strape will exercise), and (3) the extension/skill/package-manager trust model in SECURITY.md and docs/extensions.md's 'Extensions run with your full system permissions' warnings, since that (not branding) is the actual place where imported third-party code executes.
